tasks.short: Review logs for proper web system performance

steps.what: Select log sources, review period and relevant performance checks
Retrieve and filter operating system or application log records
Summarise log counts and available performance measures in the monitoring dashboard
Analyze the log snapshot and decide whether performance needs investigation

tasks.design: Configure {OTHER} monitoring queries to retrieve known log formats and calculate selected counts or measures. The administrator checks completeness and interprets the snapshot; missing data is displayed as missing, never as proof of healthy performance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Regular reviews can repeat the same filtering and counting across log sources.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved queries and dashboards can reuse an explicit review specification.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising a genuine performance problem behind incomplete or noisy events.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator relates observations to expected service behaviour and recent changes.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated log manipulation, with investigation decisions still human.

reach.learn: Explain event provenance and missing-data limits

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: monitoring systems can filter known log schemas and aggregate explicit fields without judging root cause or service health.

assumptions: Boundary is regular log checking and identifying investigation needs; incident diagnosis and correction are separately counted.

Existing operating system and application logging producers emit timestamp, source, event or status code and only measures actually available, such as response duration. Administrator specifies source paths, schema version, time zone, period and selected measures in s1's 20 hours; schema and parser upkeep is counted below. Missing or unsupported formats stop the affected query and require manual review, not inferred fields.
Test native saved queries first; the 50% manipulation share is conditional on observed manual retrieval and aggregation, not existing collection runtime.
Retain only approved log access and necessary data; local consultation and access requirements are customer facts.
research_questions: Can saved queries reproduce a manual review while visibly exposing missing sources and periods?

already_counted.description: Scope selection, source checks and specification capture

incremental.description: Query maintenance, schema changes and manual unsupported-log review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=50, gross=50 and net=42 after eight focal upkeep hours. Range assumes substantial repeated manual filtering and counting; already configured monitoring earns no new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train and assist people using web services

steps.what: Clarify training needs and select current Web implementation references
Prepare training examples and explanations from the selected guidance

loop.purpose: Draft explanations and examples for the specified audience
loop.input: Training brief and administrator-selected current guidance
loop.output: One draft lesson or technical assistance handout with source-linked instructions
loop.check: Administrator checks every instruction against current implementation, tries the example in a safe environment and checks that the explanation answers the stated audience question
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported steps or uncertain versions return to manual preparation, with no generated command executed automatically
loop.why_not_simpler: Use existing handouts first; adapting free-text explanations to a new audience may require language drafting rather than fixed field substitution

steps.what: Provide training and technical assistance and check user understanding

tasks.design: Use a bounded draft in {DOCS} only when existing guidance needs a new explanation or example. The administrator tests instructions, corrects the material and delivers the assistance personally; a draft is not evidence of user understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Adapting technical guidance to different users can require repeated writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting can supply a first explanation for review.
tasks.still_hard: Discovering why a user is struggling and checking whether they can apply the advice.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator adapts live help to what the person actually does.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing while retaining direct training and troubleshooting responsibility.

reach.learn: Use current guidance and recognise exceptions

evidence.claim: TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for human review; this supports reviewed support-content drafting rather than automatic training delivery.
Model knowledge: an adapted technical explanation must be checked against the actual implementation and user need.

assumptions: Boundary includes preparation and live assistance, not software changes made for the user; ad hoc help may contain little preparation and therefore little saving.

Administrator captures audience, actual question, environment version and selected guidance links in s1's 20 hours. Existing guidance owner produces source instructions; missing or contradictory sources trigger manual preparation. No inferred user-skill flag or uncounted brief is assumed.
Try native knowledge articles and existing handouts before model drafting; current retrieval runtime earns no saving.
Input excludes credentials and unnecessary personal information; examples are tried safely within s2's retained time.
research_questions: Does reviewed drafting reduce preparation time after counting example testing and rejected text?

incremental.description: Prompt, source-version upkeep and rejected drafts

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=89.5, gross=10.5 and net=6.5 after four upkeep hours. Range assumes some reusable preparation; all direct assistance and learning time remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate the adequacy of web testing routines

steps.what: Collect testing routines, requirements and known failure evidence
Evaluate coverage gaps and propose tests for uncertain behaviour

loop.purpose: Suggest evidence-linked coverage gaps and candidate validation tests
loop.input: Selected requirements, existing test definitions and known failure records
loop.output: One gap list with requirement references and candidate tests
loop.check: Administrator verifies each alleged gap against actual test behaviour, tries candidate tests and checks whether assertions distinguish correct from faulty behaviour
loop.stop: One proposal; unverifiable requirements, invented functions or circular assertions return to manual evaluation and no test suite is changed automatically
loop.why_not_simpler: Coverage counts alone do not show whether assertions test meaningful behaviour; native reports are used first but semantic gaps require reasoning

steps.what: Conclude whether testing procedures are adequate and recommend improvements

tasks.design: Use native {OTHER} test reports first and a bounded draft only for candidate semantic gaps. The administrator validates the suggested tests and writes the adequacy conclusion in {DOCS}; generated tests cannot certify their own effectiveness.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reading requirements and test assertions together can take substantial reasoning time.
tasks.enabler_now: Test-drafting tools can suggest candidate checks that a person evaluates independently.
tasks.still_hard: A passing test may assert the wrong behaviour or miss an important failure mode.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator determines whether test evidence addresses actual service risks.
tasks.altitude: More focus on the meaning of tests, with no automatic adequacy sign-off.

reach.learn: Demonstrate failure sensitivity rather than relying on coverage counts

evidence.claim: Playwright Test Agents can write test plans and tests and repair failing tests; this supports candidate test generation, not independent proof of adequacy.
Model knowledge: test effectiveness requires checking assertions against intended and faulty behaviour.

assumptions: Boundary is evaluating testing procedures; implementing accepted suite changes and release decisions are separate tasks.

Administrator selects requirement IDs and versions, test definitions, affected components and failure examples in s1's 30 hours. Requirement owner and existing test repository produce the original records. Missing requirements cause manual clarification; s2's retained 28 hours include executing candidate checks and recording validation outcomes before s3.
Use native coverage and test reports before model reasoning; existing test runtime is not human saving.
No generated adequacy score or auto-release threshold is introduced.
research_questions: Do suggested gaps survive independent review and expose faults missed by existing tests?

already_counted.description: Semantic gap checks and candidate-test validation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=88, gross=12 and net=6 after six upkeep hours. Range assumes useful gap suggestions after independent validation; the adequacy decision stays fully human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inform users about web problems and updates

steps.what: Confirm problem or update facts and select the user notification audience
Populate the user notice template from confirmed notification fields
Check and approve the exact notice and recipient snapshot
Send the approved problem or update notice and record delivery outcomes

tasks.design: Populate a fixed {DOCS} notice from administrator-confirmed facts and send it through {EMAIL} only after approval of the exact message and recipient snapshot. Changed facts or audience invalidate approval; delivery failures return to the administrator.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same confirmed status can be copied into a notice and then repeatedly addressed or sent.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and approved-send workflows can reuse explicit fields.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding what is known, who is affected and whether an explanation could mislead users.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator judges clarity, impact and what remains uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting and dispatch work, with message and audience responsibility unchanged.

reach.task: Use a confirmed status notice when answering users
reach.learn: Distinguish confirmed facts from an unresolved estimate

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: notice templates and approved-send workflows can reuse explicit status and recipient fields without generating an explanation or judging incident resolution.

assumptions: Boundary is user notification, excluding diagnosing or resolving the incident and implementing the update; users' reading and response effort are unchanged.

Administrator captures record ID, service, confirmed status, impact wording, approved workaround or change description, timestamp and selected recipient-group IDs in s1's 35 hours. Existing directory expands those selected groups to a recipient snapshot during s1, which the administrator checks in s3. Missing facts or unreliable recipients stop the workflow for manual composition and dispatch; no automatic resolved flag is assumed.
Test native templates and approved-send configuration before code; savings require actual manual formatting and dispatch, not existing mail transport runtime.
Approval is bound to the complete message and audience; the workflow does not invent resolution times or silently broaden distribution.
research_questions: Can a dry run preserve the approved facts and audience while reducing manual dispatch touches?

already_counted.description: Fact wording, audience capture and snapshot selection

approvals.approved_version: Exact message hash, source record version, recipient snapshot, attachments and send time approved in s3; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60, gross=40 and net=34 after six focal upkeep hours. Range assumes partly manual notice formatting and repeated dispatch; confirmed wording and audience review retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Review meaningful performance and test evidence while reducing repeated log manipulation and approved-notice dispatch.
reach: Give service desk staff reliable status information
Challenge weak tests with test engineers
skills_to_grow: Check the meaning of generated explanations
role.ambitious_version: A web administrator who spends less time assembling routine evidence and more time deciding what that evidence actually supports.
